slides.title: Rules on the wall
slides.text: Inside the post office door hangs a board of rules anyone may read. The rules say what post staff may open, what they must never open, and who to tell when something is wrong.

slides.title: School rules and app rules
slides.text: Your school has internet rules, and every app has rules too, called its agreement. Agreements say what may be posted, what is never allowed, and what happens when a rule is broken.

slides.title: The law protects your work
slides.text: Your drawing is yours, and the law protects it, just like it protects your private facts. Rules and laws are not only limits. They are layers that guard people and their work.
slides.alt: Would you rather use a picture someone else made and credit them, or draw your own from scratch?

focus.cue: Use a picture, credit its maker
Draw your own, even if it is worse

slides.title: Whose rule is it?
slides.text: Three problems land on Pim's desk in one morning. Match each one to the rule that covers it.
steps: A drawing shared without a yes: the law protects its maker
Mean posts in a class app: the agreement and school rules
A stranger reading private post: the post office wall rules

slides.title: A rule broken against you
slides.text: If someone breaks the rules against you, that is never your fault and never yours to fix alone. A broken rule is a reason to tell a trusted adult, who must act.
slides.alt: The mean message, reported: do not join in, a kind word to Pip helps more, and save it and tell an adult.

focus.cue: A mean message breaks the chat rules
Not yours to fix alone: save it and tell an adult

slides.text: Open Would You Rather at Online: share or keep. For each choice, name the rule that helps you decide.
